topics.t: Women’s reservation and delimitation: government plans a special session
topics.news: The government is planning a special session of Parliament to pass a Constitution amendment that links one-third reservation for women to delimitation, and is reported to be confident of the numbers. An earlier Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 did not secure the special majority needed in the Lok Sabha at a special sitting on 17 April. The proposals would use the 2011 Census and raise the number of Lok Sabha seats by about 50%. The Opposition has said it will oppose the delimitation provisions.

rows: A Constitution Amendment Bill needs a majority of the total membership of each House and two-thirds of the members present and voting.
A uniform rise for all States keeps each State’s share of Lok Sabha seats unchanged, which addresses worries of southern States about losing weight.
The 106th Amendment of 2023 reserves one-third of seats for women, to take effect after delimitation that follows the first Census after its commencement.

ul: **Opposition stand:** it is argued that women’s reservation should apply to the present 543 seats without being tied to delimitation.
**Way forward:** consensus on the seat formula and on timing before the 2029 general elections.

prel.d: The task of fixing the boundaries and the number of seats of territorial constituencies, done by a Delimitation Commission whose orders have the force of law.
The provision that lays down how the Constitution is amended.
The Act of 2023 that provides one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.

qs.q: Examine the concerns over linking women’s reservation to delimitation. How can federal balance be protected while expanding the Lok Sabha?

topics.t: G.V. Mavalankar: birth anniversary of the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha
topics.news: The birth anniversary of Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar, the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha, falls on 27 November. He is remembered for setting the traditions of the office of the Speaker.

rows: Born at Baroda; elected Speaker of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1946 and became the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha in 1952, serving until his death in 1956.
Elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members; decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill; has a casting vote only in a tie.

ul: **Why it matters:** the office of the Speaker is central to the neutral conduct of parliamentary business.

prel.d: The presiding officer of the Lok Sabha, elected under Article 93.

qs.q: Discuss the role of the Speaker in ensuring the effective functioning of the Lok Sabha.

topics.t: COP31 Adaptation Fund pledges fall short of annual target
topics.news: At the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, six donors announced about 50 million US dollars for the Adaptation Fund, with Spain, Germany and Ireland giving the largest sums. This is roughly one-sixth of the fund’s yearly target of at least 300 million dollars, and several wealthy countries made no new pledge.

rows: Set up under the Kyoto Protocol to finance adaptation projects in developing countries; it now also serves the Paris Agreement.
A 2% share of the proceeds of Clean Development Mechanism credits, which has dried up as carbon credit sales fell.
Developed countries should meet their climate finance obligations under the Paris Agreement and increase public finance for adaptation.
Adaptation needs of developing countries are many times larger than flows.

ul: **Why it matters:** adaptation finance decides how well vulnerable communities cope with floods, heat and sea-level rise.

prel.d: Money spent to reduce the damage from climate impacts, such as flood defences and drought-resistant crops.
A Kyoto Protocol scheme that allowed emission-reduction projects in developing countries to earn tradable credits.

qs.q: Why does adaptation finance lag behind mitigation finance? Suggest ways to strengthen it.

topics.t: Pre-Budget consultations for the Union Budget 2027–28
topics.news: The Finance Minister began pre-Budget consultations for 2027–28 on 16 November with economists and held further rounds with stakeholders from manufacturing, information technology, infrastructure, energy and sustainability. Inputs focus on tax relief, jobs, private investment and growth ahead of the Budget, which is customarily presented on 1 February.

rows: Article 112 requires the government to lay before Parliament a statement of estimated receipts and expenditure each year.
Demands for grants are voted in the Lok Sabha only; expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund is discussed but not voted.
Authorises withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund; the Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes.
Medium-term fiscal policy, macro-economic framework and medium-term expenditure statements are laid with the Budget.

ul: **Why it matters:** consultations bring sector concerns into tax and spending choices before they are finalised.

prel.d: The fund into which all government revenues and loans go and from which expenditure is met, under Article 266.
The excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings.

qs.q: Explain the stages of the Union Budget cycle. How do pre-Budget consultations improve policy making?

topics.t: World Chess Championship: Gukesh against Sindarov in Geneva
topics.news: The 2026 World Chess Championship match between the defending champion D. Gukesh of India and the challenger Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan is under way in Geneva. It is played over up to 14 classical games, and a player needs 7.5 points to win; a 7–7 tie goes to tiebreaks.

rows: Up to 14 classical games with a rest day after every three games.
Won the 2024 Candidates and then beat Ding Liren of China 7.5 to 6.5 to become the youngest world champion.
Won the 2025 World Cup and the 2026 Candidates tournament.
A museum at Cologny near Geneva; the first title match in Switzerland since 2004.

ul: **Why it matters:** India’s growing profile in chess and the role of sport in soft power.

prel.d: The event whose winner earns the right to challenge the reigning world champion.
The International Chess Federation, the world governing body for chess.

qs.q: Discuss how sports achievements contribute to India’s soft power.

topics.t: RBI lowers the daily minimum CRR maintenance back to 90 per cent
topics.news: The Reserve Bank of India has reduced the minimum daily cash reserve ratio (CRR) balance that scheduled banks must hold from 99 per cent to 90 per cent of the prescribed requirement, starting with the fortnight that begins on 1 December 2026. The change reverses the rise made from the fortnight beginning 16 October 2026. The central bank said it acted after reviewing the prevailing and evolving macroeconomic and liquidity conditions. The requirement that the average balance over the whole fortnight must meet the prescribed CRR is unchanged.

rows: Share of a bank’s net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) that must be kept as cash with the Reserve Bank; banks earn no interest on it.
The portion of the prescribed CRR that must be held on every single day of the fortnight; now 90 per cent, down from 99 per cent.
The average daily balance over the reporting fortnight must still reach the full prescribed CRR.
Section 42 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934; the 2006 amendment removed the earlier statutory floor and ceiling on the rate.
Banks gain room to manage day-to-day cash flows, which eases pressure on short-term money markets when liquidity is tight.

ul: **Why it matters:** this is a liquidity-management step, not a change in the CRR rate or the policy rate, and it shows how the central bank fine-tunes liquidity between policy meetings.

prel.d: Part of deposits that banks must keep with the central bank in cash.
Net demand and time liabilities, the base on which reserve ratios are calculated.
A situation in which banks collectively need to borrow from the central bank.

qs.q: Distinguish between quantitative and qualitative tools of monetary policy. Examine how changes in reserve requirements affect liquidity and credit.

topics.t: SEBI opens physically settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives to foreign portfolio investors
topics.news: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has issued a circular allowing foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to trade non-agricultural commodity derivative contracts that are settled by physical delivery, in addition to the cash-settled contracts they could already trade. The new framework takes effect from 1 June 2027. FPIs may hold such positions only until the tender or delivery period begins; before then they must close or roll over, and a safeguard mechanism applies to those who do not. Options on goods are not covered. The step follows a board decision taken in September 2026 and a consultation paper issued in August 2026.

rows: A foreign entity that invests in a country’s financial assets without taking management control.
Settled by paying the price difference; no goods change hands. This was the only non-agricultural access FPIs had.
Ends with actual delivery of the commodity, so a holder who stays in the contract must take or make delivery.
The window before expiry in which delivery is organised; FPIs must be out of the position before it starts.
Commodity derivatives come under SEBI since the Forward Markets Commission was merged into it in 2015.
Deeper institutional participation and better liquidity in the commodity derivatives segment.

ul: **Why it matters:** foreign institutions can help price discovery in metals and energy, but physical delivery rules are kept away from them to avoid logistic and warehousing risks.
**Watch:** agricultural commodities remain outside this opening, reflecting food-price sensitivity.

prel.d: A contract whose value is derived from a commodity price, such as a futures contract.
The process by which markets arrive at a price through buyers and sellers’ trades.
Closing a near-expiry contract and opening a later-dated one.

qs.q: How do derivatives markets help in price discovery? Discuss the case for and the risks of opening commodity derivatives to foreign investors.

topics.t: Indian Ocean Rim Association: 25th Council of Ministers meets in New Delhi
topics.news: Foreign ministers and heads of delegation of the 23 member states of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) met in New Delhi for the grouping’s 25th Council of Ministers, with India in the chair. The Prime Minister met the visiting leaders. The External Affairs Minister said the Indian Ocean matters for trade, energy security, connectivity and prosperity, and urged IORA to strengthen its collective voice and practical cooperation amid geopolitical change. India, as chair, is guided by its vision of MAHASAGAR.

rows: Regional organisation of Indian Ocean littoral states, formed in 1997 as the Indian Ocean Rim Initiative and renamed in 2013; secretariat at Ebene, Mauritius.
23 member states, with a wider set of dialogue partners from outside the region.
Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions, a vision announced by India in Mauritius in March 2025.
SAGAR, Security and Growth for All in the Region, announced in 2015.

Maritime safety and security, trade and investment facilitation, fisheries, disaster risk management, science and technology, tourism and culture; blue economy and women’s empowerment cut across them.
The highest decision-making body, meeting once a year.

ul: **Why it matters:** the Indian Ocean carries a large share of world trade and energy flows, and chairing IORA lets India shape the regional agenda on maritime security and the blue economy.
**Link:** the meeting complements India’s Indo-Pacific initiatives and its outreach to the Global South.

prel.d: A state with a coastline on a given sea or ocean.
Sustainable use of ocean resources for growth, jobs and livelihoods.
A non-member country that takes part in an organisation’s dialogue process.

qs.q: Discuss the strategic importance of the Indian Ocean Region for India. How can regional groupings like IORA advance India’s interests?

topics.t: Supreme Court takes up contempt over the Thiruparankundram lamp-lighting order
topics.news: A Supreme Court bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi issued contempt notices to Tamil Nadu’s Chief Secretary, the Director General of Police, the Madurai Collector and others for not carrying out its order on lighting the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon on Thiruparankundram hill. The Chief Secretary must appear in person and file an affidavit on communications between officials. The Court suspended the trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple, ordered the lamp to be lit the next day, and handed the security of the temple and hill to the Central Reserve Police Force. It said an order of the Court is binding and not open to negotiation.

rows: Wilful disobedience of a court order (civil contempt) or acts that lower the court’s authority or obstruct justice (criminal contempt).
Article 129 makes the Supreme Court a court of record with power to punish its own contempt; Article 215 does so for High Courts; the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 regulates the law.
Lets the Court pass any order necessary to do complete justice in a matter before it.
Requires all civil and judicial authorities in India to act in aid of the Supreme Court.
The lamp was lit only at the customary mandapam on 24 November despite the Court’s permission for the Deepathoon; the State had earlier apologised.
Thiruparankundram is among the six principal shrines of Murugan in Tamil Nadu.

ul: **Why it matters:** the case tests enforcement of judicial orders against executive authorities, and the use of Central forces where a State is held to have failed.
**Caution:** the temple dispute also involves the balance between religious custom, public order and Article 25 rights.

prel.d: A court whose proceedings are kept as permanent record and which can punish for its own contempt.
Wilful disobedience of a judgment, order or undertaking given to a court.
Directs authorities to assist the Supreme Court in enforcing its orders.

qs.q: Examine the constitutional basis and limits of the contempt power of the higher judiciary. How can compliance with court orders by the executive be ensured?

topics.t: Power Ministers’ Conference: planning for generation, storage and distribution
topics.news: A two-day conference of Power Ministers began in New Delhi on 27 November, chaired by Union Power Minister Manohar Lal, with representatives of 28 States and 8 Union Territories and electricity regulators. The agenda covers integrated planning across generation, storage, transmission and distribution, smart metering, the finances of distribution companies, and the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme. Officials said the sector offers investment potential of about ₹200 lakh crore over two decades. The Power Secretary put installed capacity at about 563 GW, with over 55 per cent from non-fossil sources, and said around 60 GW was added in the last 12 months, 87 per cent of it non-fossil.

rows: Electricity is in the Concurrent List, so the Centre and States share responsibility.
About 563 GW, of which more than 55 per cent is non-fossil.
About 60 GW in the past 12 months, with 87 per cent non-fossil.
Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme, launched in 2021 to cut losses of distribution companies through smart meters and network upgrades.
State distribution companies; the conference noted a positive profit after tax in 2024-25.
Resource adequacy, energy storage, inter-State and intra-State transmission, and nuclear power sites.

ul: **Why it matters:** the energy transition needs coordinated Centre-State action on storage, grids and distribution finances.
**Next:** a joint session with the Forum of Regulators and State regulatory commissions is planned for 28 November.

prel.d: Ensuring enough generation and storage to meet peak demand reliably.
A meter that records consumption digitally and communicates it to the utility.
Electricity distribution company that supplies power to consumers.

qs.q: What are the challenges before India’s power distribution sector? Discuss how Centre-State coordination can support the energy transition.

topics.t: Allahabad High Court quashes the UPPSC PCS-2025 preliminary exam result
topics.news: A single-judge bench of the Allahabad High Court, headed by Justice Manish Kumar Nigam, set aside the result of the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission’s PCS-2025 preliminary examination and directed the Commission to prepare and declare a fresh result before the remaining stages go ahead. The petition by four candidates challenged certain provisions of the recruitment advertisement; the drive is for 814 posts. The decision is expected to benefit candidates in reserved categories. Detailed reasons are in the judgment.

rows: The State Public Service Commission of Uttar Pradesh, a constitutional body under Article 315.
High Courts can issue writs under Article 226 for fundamental rights and for any other purpose.
Chairman and members of a State commission are appointed by the Governor but removed only by the President.
Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in public employment and permits reservation.
The remedy ordered is a fresh preliminary result, not a cancellation of the recruitment.
814 posts are being filled through the exam.

ul: **Why it matters:** recruitment disputes show how courts police fairness and reservation rules in public hiring.
**Note:** a challenge to the order may still be made before a larger bench or the Supreme Court.

prel.d: Provides for Public Service Commissions for the Union and States.
An order quashing a decision of a lower authority.
The screening stage of the civil services selection process.

qs.q: Discuss the role of Public Service Commissions in ensuring merit and fairness in recruitment. How do courts review recruitment processes?

topics.t: Hunger Hotspots: sixteen countries at risk of worsening food insecurity
topics.news: The Food and Agriculture Organization and the World Food Programme have warned in their Hunger Hotspots report that acute hunger will worsen in 16 countries over the next six months. Sudan, Yemen, South Sudan, Somalia and northern Nigeria are the five places of highest concern, and all have featured on the list repeatedly since 2022. In Sudan, famine risk is expected to continue in 13 areas of North Darfur and South Kordofan, with war and an El Niño-linked drought both affecting food production. Gaza moved down one level after the October 2025 ceasefire, yet 67 per cent of its people still face crisis-level hunger or worse.

rows: A twice-yearly early-warning report of the two Rome-based UN agencies on places where acute food insecurity may deteriorate.
Sudan, Yemen, South Sudan, Somalia and northern Nigeria.
The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification has five phases; Phase 5 is Catastrophe or Famine.
At least 20 per cent of households with extreme food shortage, 30 per cent child acute malnutrition and two deaths per 10,000 a day.
Conflict, climate shocks such as drought, economic stress and funding gaps.
Won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020 for efforts against hunger.

ul: **Why it matters:** the report guides humanitarian funding and links to Sustainable Development Goal 2, Zero Hunger.
**India link:** India has sent food assistance to several countries in need and backs the global food-security agenda.

prel.d: Hunger that threatens lives or livelihoods at a specific time, regardless of cause.
The most extreme phase of food insecurity, declared when set thresholds are crossed.
Goal to end hunger and achieve food security by 2030.

qs.q: Conflict and climate change are driving global hunger. Examine the role of international organisations and India in addressing food insecurity.

topics.t: India presents its 2036 Olympic bid vision to the IOC Future Host Commission
topics.news: India presented its vision and proposed roadmap for hosting the 2036 Olympic and Paralympic Games to the International Olympic Committee’s Future Host Commission in an online interaction of about 30 minutes, followed by a short discussion. Ahmedabad is the proposed host city. The Commission is led by Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic and has nine members. Seven countries are in the race: India, Germany, Hungary, Qatar, South Korea, South Africa and Türkiye. The IOC’s public survey on India’s bid is expected in the third week of December and the evaluation in March, which will begin the Strategic Dialogue phase.

rows: IOC panel that studies interest from prospective hosts and advises the Executive Board.
Germany, Hungary, Qatar, South Korea, South Africa and Türkiye.
Public opinion survey in December and an evaluation in March that opens the Strategic Dialogue phase.
The host is finally chosen by a vote of IOC members at a Session.
India hosted the Asian Games in 1951 and 1982 and the Commonwealth Games in 2010, all in Delhi.

ul: **Why it matters:** hosting needs large investment in infrastructure and sport systems, and can help urban development and soft power if costs are controlled.
**Debate:** critics point to cost overruns and the need for public benefit beyond the event.

prel.d: International Olympic Committee, based in Lausanne, Switzerland.
Multi-sport event for athletes with disabilities.
The IOC phase of detailed talks with interested hosts after initial evaluation.

qs.q: Assess the costs and benefits of hosting a mega sporting event like the Olympics for a developing country such as India.

topics.t: Project Cheetah: population reaches 62 after two litters at Kuno
topics.news: India’s cheetah population has risen to 62 after nine cubs were born at Kuno National Park in October and November 2026: five on 5 October to an India-born female, and four on 20 November to KOMG 3, the first Botswana-origin female to give birth in India. About 43 of the animals are India-born. The count sits at the lower end of the target of 60 to 70 cheetahs across the Kuno–Gandhi Sagar landscape by 2032. It is cautioned that births alone do not show a self-sustaining population; cub survival beyond a year and breeding by wild-born animals are the real tests.

rows: Launched on 17 September 2022 with eight cheetahs from Namibia at Kuno; 12 more came from South Africa in February 2023 and nine from Botswana in February 2026.
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change through the National Tiger Conservation Authority.
Kuno National Park, Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary and, since October 2026, Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve, all in Madhya Pradesh.
The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952.
A self-sustaining metapopulation of 60 to 70 animals by 2032 over about 17,000 sq km.
Over 450 Cheetah Mitras across 80 villages and a share of eco-tourism income for nearby villages.

ul: **Why it matters:** this is the first intercontinental translocation of a large wild carnivore for reintroduction, so its success shapes future rewilding.
**Challenges:** prey base, space, disease, human-wildlife conflict and the narrow founder gene pool.

prel.d: A set of connected sub-populations of one species that exchange individuals.
Restoring a species or ecosystem to a place it has been lost from.
The first group from which a new population grows.

qs.q: Evaluate the progress and challenges of Project Cheetah. What lessons does it offer for species reintroduction in India?

topics.t: India’s forex reserves fall to $700.9 billion
topics.news: India’s foreign exchange reserves declined by $4.4 billion to $700.9 billion in the week ended 20 November, data released on 27 November show. The fall in gold, down by over $4 billion to $94.5 billion, accounted for most of the drop. Foreign currency assets slipped $266 million to $583.2 billion, special drawing rights by $67 million to $18.45 billion, and the reserve position with the IMF by $15 million to $4.74 billion.

rows: Largest component, mainly foreign securities and deposits; moves with exchange-rate valuation and central bank operations.
$94.5 billion in the latest week; its value moves with global bullion prices.
The IMF’s reserve asset, created in 1969, held at $18.45 billion.
Part of India’s quota that can be drawn without conditions; $4.74 billion.
The Reserve Bank publishes the data weekly for the week ended Friday.
Cover for imports, a cushion against capital outflows and a tool to smooth rupee volatility.

ul: **Why it matters:** reserves signal external-sector strength and the central bank’s capacity to manage volatility.
**Note:** much of a weekly change reflects valuation of gold and currencies, not only purchases or sales.

prel.d: An international reserve asset issued by the IMF.
Change in reserve value from price and exchange-rate movements.
Resources a member can draw from the IMF without conditions.

qs.q: What are the components and functions of foreign exchange reserves? Discuss how their adequacy is assessed.

topics.t: RBI Governor on AI and the role of MSMEs in a developed India
topics.news: Speaking at an SME finance summit in Mumbai on 27 November, the Reserve Bank Governor said artificial intelligence could add an estimated $600 to 700 billion of economic value for the MSME sector and that a developed India cannot be built by large firms alone. He cited MSME contributions of about 31 per cent of GDP, 35 per cent of manufacturing output, nearly half of merchandise exports and jobs for over 45 crore people. He said self-reliance and resilient supply chains open chances in electronics, semiconductors, defence and clean energy, and trade pacts with the UK and the European Union can widen market access. He also inaugurated an SME finance facilitation centre.

rows: About 31 per cent of GDP, 35 per cent of manufacturing and nearly half of exports.
More than 45 crore people, per the Governor’s figures.
An estimated $600–700 billion of value for the sector.
Electronics, semiconductors, defence and clean energy.
Free trade agreements can give cheaper inputs and larger export markets.
Access to credit remains the central issue for small enterprises.

ul: **Why it matters:** MSMEs are central to jobs, exports and supply chains, so credit and technology access shape growth.
**Link:** MSMEs are classified by investment and turnover limits under the MSME Development Act, 2006.

prel.d: Micro, small and medium enterprises classified by investment and turnover.
The sequence of activities that turn inputs into final goods.
Online registration of MSMEs in India.

qs.q: Examine the role of MSMEs in India’s growth and the constraints they face. How can technology and credit reforms help?

topics.t: Indian researchers develop stable white LEDs using perovskite nanocrystals
topics.news: Researchers at the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences, Bengaluru, an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology, with IIT Delhi, have devised a way to stop colour blurring in white light-emitting diodes made from halide perovskite nanocrystals. In such devices halide ions drift between neighbouring nanocrystals and turn the intended colours into unwanted shades within minutes. The team treated the surface with lead selenide to reduce vacancies and added an ultrathin alumina layer of about 5 to 6 nm by atomic layer deposition as a barrier. The devices gave stable white light for up to 24 hours, and the tone could be shifted from cool to warm by changing current. Lead toxicity remains a concern.

rows: Tiny crystals of a halide perovskite structure that emit pure, bright colours cheaply.
Migration of halide ions between crystals, which mixes colours.
A technique that builds ultrathin, uniform coatings one atomic layer at a time.
Lead selenide surface treatment plus an alumina barrier layer.
Stable white light for up to 24 hours, tunable from cooler to warmer tones.
Lead content needs greener alternatives before commercial use.

ul: **Why it matters:** efficient, low-cost lighting and displays reduce energy use and support India’s electronics ambitions.
**Background:** the 2014 Nobel Prize in Physics recognised the invention of efficient blue LEDs, which made white LED lighting possible.

prel.d: A semiconductor device that emits light when current passes through it.
A material with structures at the scale of billionths of a metre.
A crystal family with halide ions such as chloride, bromide or iodide.

qs.q: How are advances in nanomaterials and semiconductors relevant to India’s energy efficiency and electronics manufacturing goals?
